{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''quotient''' (also called '''Serre quotient''' or '''Gabriel quotient''') of an [[abelian category]] <math>\mathcal{A}</math> by a [[Serre subcategory]] <math>\mathcal{B}</math> is the abelian category <math>\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B}</math> which, intuitively, is obtained from <math>\mathcal{A}</math> by ignoring (i.e. treating as [[Zero-object|zero]]) all [[Object (category theory)|objects]] from <math>\mathcal{B}</math>.  There is a canonical [[Exact functor|exact]] [[functor]] <math>Q \colon \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B}</math> whose kernel is <math>\mathcal B</math>, and <math>\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B}</math> is in a certain sense the most general abelian category with this property. 

Forming Serre quotients of abelian categories is thus formally akin to forming [[Quotient group|quotients of groups]]. Serre quotients are somewhat similar to [[Quotient category|quotient categories]], the difference being that with Serre quotients all involved categories are abelian and all functors are exact. Serre quotients also often have the character of [[Localization of a category|localizations of categories]], especially if the Serre subcategory is [[Localizing subcategory|localizing]].

== Definition ==
Formally, <math>\mathcal A/\mathcal B</math> is the [[Category (mathematics)|category]] whose objects are those of <math>\mathcal A</math> and whose [[morphism]]s from ''X'' to ''Y'' are given by the [[direct limit]] (of [[abelian group]]s) 

<math display="block">\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A/\mathcal B}(X,Y):=\varinjlim \mathrm{Hom}_\mathcal A(X', Y/Y')</math> 

where the limit is taken over [[subobject]]s <math>X' \subseteq X</math> and <math>Y' \subseteq Y</math> such that <math>X/X'\in \cal{B}</math> and <math>Y' \in \cal{B}</math>.  (Here, <math>X/X'</math> and <math>Y/Y'</math> denote [[quotient object]]s computed in <math>\mathcal A</math>.) These pairs of subobjects are ordered by <math>(X',Y')\preccurlyeq(X'',Y'') \Longleftrightarrow X''\subseteq X' \text{ and } Y'\subseteq Y''</math>.

Composition of morphisms in <math>\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B}</math> is induced by the [[universal property]] of the direct limit.

The canonical functor <math>Q \colon \mathcal A \to \mathcal A/\mathcal B</math> sends an object ''X'' to itself and a morphism <math>f \colon X \to Y</math> to the corresponding element of the direct limit with ''X′'' = X and ''Y′'' = 0.

An alternative, equivalent construction of the quotient category uses what is called a "[[Localization of a category|calculus of fractions]]" to define the morphisms of <math>\mathcal A/\mathcal B</math>. Here, one starts with the class <math>S</math> of those morphisms in <math>\mathcal A</math> whose kernel and cokernel both belong to <math>\mathcal{B}</math>. This is a multiplicative system in the sense of Gabriel-Zisman, and one can localize the category <math>\mathcal A</math> at the system <math>S</math> to obtain <math>\mathcal A/\mathcal B:=\mathcal A[S^{-1}]</math>.<ref>[https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02MN Section 12.10] ''The Stacks Project''</ref>

== Examples ==
Let <math>k</math> be a [[Field (mathematics)|field]] and consider the abelian category <math>{\rm Mod}(k)</math> of all [[vector space]]s over <math>k</math>. Then the full subcategory <math>{\rm mod}(k)</math> of finite-[[dimension]]al vector spaces is a Serre-subcategory of <math>{\rm Mod}(k)</math>. The Serre quotient <math>\cal{C} = {\rm Mod}(k)/{\rm mod}(k)</math> has as objects the <math>k</math>-vector spaces, and the set of morphisms from <math>X</math> to <math>Y</math> in <math>\cal{C}</math> is <math display="block">\{k\text{-linear maps from } X \text{ to } Y\}/\{k\text{-linear maps from } X \text{ to } Y \text{ with finite-dimensional image}\}</math> (which is a [[Quotient space (linear algebra)|quotient of vector spaces]]).  This has the effect of identifying all finite-dimensional vector spaces with 0, and of identifying two [[linear map]]s whenever their difference has finite-dimensional [[Image (mathematics)|image]].  This example shows that the Serre quotient can behave like a [[quotient category]].

For another example, take the [[Category of abelian groups|abelian category '''Ab''' of all abelian groups]] and the Serre subcategory of all [[Torsion abelian group|torsion abelian groups]]. The Serre quotient here is [[Equivalence of categories|equivalent]] to the category <math>\operatorname{Mod}(\Bbb{Q})</math> of all vector spaces over the rationals, with the canonical functor <math>\mathbf{Ab}\to\operatorname{Mod}(\Bbb{Q})</math> given by tensoring with <math>\Bbb{Q}</math>. Similarly, the Serre quotient of the category of finitely generated abelian groups by the subcategory of finitely generated torsion groups is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional vectorspaces over <math>\Bbb{Q}</math>.<ref>{{Cite web |title=109.76 The category of modules modulo torsion modules |url=https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B0J |website=The Stacks Project}}</ref> Here, the Serre quotient behaves like a [[Localization of a category|localization]].

== Properties ==
The Serre quotient <math>\mathcal A/\mathcal B</math> is an abelian category, and the canonical functor <math>Q \colon \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B}</math> is [[Exact functor|exact]] and surjective on objects.  The kernel of <math>Q</math> is <math>\mathcal B</math>, i.e., <math>Q(X)</math> is [[Zero-object|zero]] in <math>\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{B}</math> if and only if <math>X</math> belongs to <math>\mathcal{B}</math>.

The Serre quotient and canonical functor are characterized by the following [[universal property]]: if <math>\mathcal C</math> is any abelian category and <math>F \colon \mathcal A \to \mathcal C</math> is an exact functor such that <math>F(X)</math> is a zero in ''<math>\mathcal C</math>'' for each object <math>X \in \mathcal B</math>, then there is a unique exact functor <math>\overline{F} \colon \mathcal A/\mathcal B \to \mathcal C</math> such that <math>F = \overline{F} \circ Q</math>.<ref>Gabriel, Pierre, ''[http://www.numdam.org/article/BSMF_1962__90__323_0.pdf Des categories abeliennes]'', Bull. Soc. Math. France '''90''' (1962), 323-448.</ref>

Given three abelian categories <math>\mathcal{A}</math>, <math>\mathcal{B}</math>, <math>\mathcal{C}</math>, we have 
:<math>\mathcal A/\mathcal B \cong \mathcal C</math>
if and only if 
:there exists an exact and [[Essentially surjective functor|essentially surjective]] functor <math>F \colon \mathcal A \to \mathcal C</math> whose kernel is <math>\mathcal{B}</math> and such that for every morphism <math>f:FX\to FY</math> in <math>\mathcal C</math> there exist morphisms <math>\phi:W\to X</math> and <math>\psi:W\to Y</math> in <math>\mathcal A</math> so that <math>F\phi</math> is an isomorphism and <math>f=(F\psi)\circ(F\phi)^{-1}</math>.

== Theorems involving Serre quotients ==

=== Serre's description of coherent sheaves on a projective scheme ===
According to a theorem by [[Jean-Pierre Serre]], the category <math>\operatorname{coh}(X)</math> of [[Coherent sheaf|coherent sheaves]] on a projective scheme <math>X=\operatorname{Proj}(R)</math> (where <math>R</math> is a commutative [[Noetherian ring|noetherian]] [[graded ring]], graded by the non-negative integers and generated by degree-0 and finitely many degree-1 elements, and <math>\operatorname{Proj}(R)</math> refers to the [[Proj construction]]) can be described as the Serre quotient

<math display="block">\operatorname{coh}(X) \cong \operatorname{mod}^\Bbb{Z}(R)\ / \ \operatorname{mod}_{\mathrm{tor}}^\Bbb{Z}(R)</math>

where <math>\operatorname{mod}^\Bbb{Z}(R)</math> denotes the category of finitely-generated graded modules over <math>R</math> and <math>\operatorname{mod}_{\mathrm{tor}}^\Bbb{Z}(R)</math> is the Serre subcategory consisting of all those graded modules <math>M</math> which are 0 in all degrees that are high enough, i.e. for which there exists <math>n_0\in\Bbb{N}</math> such that <math>M_n=0</math> for all <math>n\geq n_0</math>.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Görtz |first1=Ulrich |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=do7zDwAAQBAJ&q=wedhorn+algebraic+geometry |title=Algebraic Geometry I: Schemes: With Examples and Exercises |last2=Wedhorn |first2=Torsten |publisher=Springer Nature |year=2020 |isbn= 9783658307332|edition=2nd |pages=381 |language=en |chapter=Remark 13.21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Proposition 30.14.4 |url=https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YR |website=The Stacks Project}}</ref>

A similar description exists for the category of [[quasi-coherent sheaves]] on <math>X=\operatorname{Proj}(R)</math>, even if <math>R</math> is not noetherian.

=== Gabriel–Popescu theorem ===
The [[Gabriel–Popescu theorem]] states that any [[Grothendieck category]] <math>\mathcal{A}</math> is [[Equivalence of categories|equivalent]] to a Serre quotient of the form <math>\operatorname{Mod}(R)/\cal{B}</math>, where <math>\operatorname{Mod}(R)</math> denotes the abelian category of right [[Module (mathematics)|modules]] over some [[unital ring]] <math>R</math>, and <math>\cal{B}</math> is some [[localizing subcategory]] of <math>\operatorname{Mod}(R)</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=N. Popesco |author2=P. Gabriel |year=1964|title=Caractérisation des catégories abéliennes avec générateurs et limites inductives exactes |journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences |volume=258 |pages=4188–4190}}</ref>

=== Quillen's localization theorem ===
[[Daniel Quillen]]'s [[algebraic K-theory]] assigns to each [[exact category]] <math>\mathcal{C}</math> a sequence of abelian groups <math>K_n(\mathcal C),\ n\geq 0</math>, and this assignment is functorial in <math>\mathcal{C}</math>. Quillen proved that, if <math>\mathcal{B}</math> is a Serre subcategory of the abelian category <math>\mathcal{A}</math>, there is a [[long exact sequence]] of the form<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Quillen |first=Daniel |date=1973 |editor-last= |editor-first= |title=Higher algebraic K-theory: I |url=https://sma.epfl.ch/~hessbell/topo_alg/Quillen.pdf |journal=Higher K-Theories |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |volume=341 |language=en |location= |publisher=Springer |pages=85–147 |doi=10.1007/BFb0067053 |isbn=978-3-540-06434-3 |archive-date=2022-01-28 |access-date=2022-12-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128115001/http://sma.epfl.ch/~hessbell/topo_alg/Quillen.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

<math display="block">\cdots \to K_n(\mathcal B) \to K_n(\mathcal A) \to K_n(\mathcal {A/B})\to K_{n-1}(\mathcal B)\to\cdots\to K_0(\mathcal {A/B})\to 0 </math>
